newsitem.title: CANADA: AZCO cleared to seek Indonesian contract.
newsitem.headline: AZCO cleared to seek Indonesian contract.

text.p: AZCO Mining Inc said Monday it has been accepted by the Ministry of Mines of Indonesia to apply for a contract on Irian Jaya.
The contract was applied for under agreement with Indotan Inc, an Indonesian firm that acted as agent on behalf of AZCO.
AZCO paid $416,750 as security for the right to work, the company said.

Indotan has retained a 15 percent participating interest. The interest is in the form of a non-interest-bearing, non-recourse loan until the completion of a favorable, bankable feasibility study, AZCO said.
Thereafter, the parties shall bear costs pro-rata in accordance with their participating interest, AZCO said.
The costs carried for Indotan's 15 percent participating interest will be repaid first out of profits, in the event of commercial production, AZCO said.
Indotan will also retain a 2 percent net smelter return royalty, which may be purchased by Azco at any time by the issuance of US$3 million, in cash or shares at the discretion of AZCO, AZCO said.

The newly acquired ground which is the subject of Azco's mineral rights is comprised of 83,350 hectares and is situated due east from Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc's Grasberg/Erzberg mine, with annual copper and gold production there expected to reach 1.1 billion pounds and 1.5 million ounces, respectively, the company said.

Filed geological reports of AZCO's ground confirm that only very limited exploration had been done previously, but several geochemical results have shown relatively high content in gold, zinc and lead, AZCO said.
A detailed geological mapping and ground geophysical survey will be considered as a first phase program of exploration, the company said.
AZCO said it is negotiating for other potential ground, geologically similar to that of the Grasberg/Erzberg area.
